s: Order a coffee and pay at a café

a.d: In São Paulo, the “cafezinho” is a sacred break: a small, strong, sweet coffee. In bakeries you order at the counter and pay at the register. Watch out for false friends: “pão” is bread (not “pan”), and “café” also means the café itself.

h.tr: Good morning! What will it be?

a.d: In Fortaleza, neighbors chat in plazas and on sidewalks in the evening. A pleasant chat starts with “Tudo bem?”, a small compliment and an invitation. Note that “Prazer em conhecer você” is polite and warm; “Foi um prazer!” works as goodbye.

Come have dinner at my place on Friday!

At eight. It was a pleasure, Sam!

s: Join a traditional Saturday feijoada lunch

a.d: In Cuiabá, Saturday lunch often means feijoada: black beans stewed with pork, served with rice, collard greens, farofa and orange slices. It is eaten slowly with family. False friend: “farofa” is toasted manioc flour, not a type of rice.

p: Today you meet Tia Neuza, from Cuiabá. Today you join a family feijoada.
